newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's LUKoil chief sees 1996 growth.
newsitem.headline: Russia's LUKoil chief sees 1996 growth.

text.p: The president of Russian oil company LUKoil said on Monday he expected key company indicators would show growth in 1996 but a number of external factors were limiting company improvement.
"Despite the unfavourable effects of many factors generally out of the company's control, we expect growth in the majority of key indicators (for all of 1996)," Vagit Alekperov said in a statement.
"There was a reduction of most consumers' ability to pay, weak domestic demand and, as a result, low domestic oil prices relative to world levels," he said.
"A high tax burden and inability to attain credit resoures during a time of increasing need for investment by the company limit the speed of quality improvement," he said.
The statement said the company would focus on improving management and optimising production, sales and financing.
OAO Neftyanaya Kompaniya LUKoil, one of about a dozen vertically integrated oil companies set up after the dissolution of the Soviet Union, is Russia's leading oil producer.

It said on Monday that its net profit for the nine months to September 30, 1996, were 2.61 trillion roubles, or $522 million, an 118 percent increase on the same period a year earlier, according to Russian accounting standards on an accruals basis.
Crude output rose to 43.6 million tonnes over the nine months from 42.9 million tonnes in the same period of 1995, it said.
